messages:
tammy (sec-eng): nightly vuln-scan failing again — GHAS runners pile up and both Trivy + Snyk jobs error with KMS decrypt failures on build artifacts. saw this last night and again this AM. logs attached below, any ideas?

kai (infra): can you paste the exact log lines? GHAS queue/backoff or runner crash? also which runner pool (self-hosted vs github-hosted)?

tammy (sec-eng): self-hosted runners (eu-prod-runners). log snippet:```
2026-03-19T23:02:11Z runner[1234]: dequeuing job 9876 -> worker spawn failed: queue depth 128, max_workers=64
2026-03-19T23:02:12Z snyk-scanner: error: failed to unwrap key for artifact 'redwood/service-x:sha256:abcd': AccessDenied: User is not authorized to perform: kms:Decrypt
```

anoop (platform-sre): KMS error stands out. we rotated a small subset of KMS keys last week for onboarding; possible IAM or key policy missed the scanner role. can you confirm the role arn the scanner uses?

tammy (sec-eng): scanner uses `arn:aws:iam::111111111111:role/redwood-scanner`. I grep'd the audit logs; saw a denied `kms:Decrypt` for that role around the same time.

kai (infra): GHAS queuing + duplicate Snyk runs are probably cascading. when a runner can't fetch artifact (KMS fail) the job times out and GHAS requeues -> triggers new Snyk job. two things: (1) add `concurrency` to GHAS workflow to avoid back-to-back duplicates, (2) exponential backoff / retry with jitter for scanner job so we don't overwhelm runners. example:```yaml
concurrency:
  group: scan-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: false
```

jess (devex): also saw a format change in the Snyk suppression export after their 1.8.0 release — our suppression adapter started dropping `cve` keys and now relies on `vulnerability.id`. that mapping mismatch made many CVEs unlabeled and re-opened as findings. patch in prod converter fixes that. sample diff:```
old: {"cve": "CVE-2025-0421", "reason": "accepted risk"}
new: {"vulnerability": {"id":"SNYK-JS-XYZ","cve":"CVE-2025-0421"}}
```

tammy (sec-eng): ah ok that explains the flurry of regressions I saw. so two separate root causes: KMS IAM regression -> job failures -> requeues, plus suppression schema drift -> reopened findings. both need fixes.

security-bot: ALERT: vuln-scan.pipeline.failure rate=6 within 15m, severity=warning :rotating_light:

anoop (platform-sre): plan: I will open a PR to re-add kms:Decrypt to `redwood-scanner` role with a scoped resource (specific key ARN) and link to the audit justification. after IAM change we should manually re-run the queued GHAS workflow once to clear duplicates.

kai (infra): I'll submit a tiny GHAS workflow patch to add `concurrency` and bump `timeout-minutes` for `run-snyk` from 30 -> 45, and add a retry wrapper:```bash
for i in 1 2 3; do snyk test || sleep $((2**i + RANDOM%3)); done
```

jess (devex): I'll update the suppression converter to handle both old/new shapes and add a unit test mapping CVE->Snyk ID. will ship as a hotfix to `devex/suppression-adapter` and create a migration job to reapply existing suppressions where cve matches.

tammy (sec-eng): can we also add an alert to perf that flags GHAS queue depth > 20 for >5m? we caught it late.

anoop (platform-sre): yes will add a CloudWatch metric/alarm and a Datadog dashboard tile.

kai (infra): i'll handle the immediate GHAS workflow PR, assign to @tammy for verification. PR link when ready.

tammy (sec-eng): thumbs up. after IAM rollback + GHAS patch + suppression migration we should re-run a full night scan and monitor. assigning owners: IAM restore -> @anoop, GHAS/workflow -> @kai, suppression adapter -> @jess.

security-bot: NOTE: incident-created id=INC-20260319-023, severity=low, owners=[anoop,kai,jess]

jess (devex): i'll add a regression test in CI that runs a smoke Snyk scan on a tiny fixture (with mocked KMS) so we catch this earlier.

tammy (sec-eng): thanks all. next update in this thread once PRs merged + re-run done. :thumbsup:
